newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity's Coffman sees U.S. economy slowing down.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity's Coffman sees U.S. economy slowing down.

text.p: The Fidelity Investments VIP High Income Portfolio manager said he expects the U.S. economy to slow down and has reduced his holdings in cyclical commodities such as paper and increased holdings in telecommunications as a result.

Barry Coffman, manager of the $1.389 billion variable insurance product fund, said in a newsletter to investment professionals, "As a result of my less-than-optimistic view of the economy, I underweighted cyclical companies...paper, steel and chemicals."

"I have zeroed in on emerging telecommunications issues in businesses such as paging, cellular, and some of the newer industries such as PCS (personal communications systems) and CLEC (Competitive Local Exchange Carriers).
The VIP High Income fund's top holdings in September were: PanAmSat Corp, Marvel Parent Holdings, Inc, Cablevision Systems Corp, and Mother's Work, Inc.
Coffman, whose fund is primarily invested in bonds, noted the spread between Treasuries and high yield bonds has narrowed "by as much as 75 basis points."

Asked if that means junk bonds are expensive in comparision, he said, "It depnds on your outlook. If we continue to march along at a pretty decent economic clip, then they're not overly expensive. However, if you think it's more likely that the U.S. economy will slow down -- which is my own personal view -- then the segment is probably fairly valued."

Fidelity on Wednesday announced an interactive software program that would allow investors to decide whether a variable rate annuity or a mutual fund would be best for them. The VIP High Income Portfolio is one of the underlying funds in the annuity program.
